There are 11 notorious WB cartoons that have been completely pulled from circulation due to "racism." Warner also put a second volume of the Tom & Jerry "Golden Collection" on hold indefinitely, due to corporate squeamishness about two cartoons in particular, His Mouse Friday and Casanova Cat. Apparently they have been none too happy with T&J fans who demand a complete and uncensored set, dismissing them as uncouth and unenlightened racists themselves who don't know better than corporate executives what is "appropriate for modern viewing audiences." The bizarre thing is that Casanova Cat wasn't even banned in Britain for showing Jerry in blackface -- it was banned for showing Tom smoking.

Then you have Disney, disgustingly SJW Hydra that it is with feminist princess films and interracial Star Wars, shoving Song of the South in the Walt Vault seemingly forever, never to see the light of day again. Why? Because black groups complained that it showed slavery in too nice of a light by depicting a slave who wasn't maltreated on the plantation. But Song of the South is just a live-action/animated version of the old Uncle Remus tales that Walt himself grew up loving so much he wanted to make into a feature-length film. Yet Disney has apparently been slow to catch up to the SJW-ing that other studios had already started falling victim to by the 1960s; the last theatrical release of Song of the South was in 1986, for the 40th anniversary release of the original film. Strangely, while the movie has been pulled from circulation (you can't even buy DVDs of it except laserdisc transfers of varying quality from foreign importers, though this one in the U.S. seems pretty good), the theme park ride still exists at Disneyland and, I believe, Epcot/Disney Euro.

Why do these dumb studios assume that adult animation collectors and fans need to be coddled like children, or that a stupid mouse in blackface isn't comparatively tame when likened to what kids can already access on the fucking Internet? I can go to Google images and pull up blackface cartoons of Obama. I can turn on Comedy Central and watch a South Park episode featuring the character Token Black (though I can't watch the Muhammad episodes... but those, at least, are available on DVD). I can pull up a porn website and watch a guy stick his fist in another guy's ass. I can watch ISIS beheading videos. But Jerry the mouse with shoe polish on his face is somehow worse???

What can be done about this? I don't give a shit what Al Sharpton or Black Lies Matter think, and just want to watch some fucking cartoons that had fuck-all to do with lynchings even in the '60s, and even less so (negative amount) today. The only "unofficial" source is YouTube, from potato-quality VHS rips that users taped from rare uncut airings in the '80s. That's not a proper release, and even then, some of the cartoons are only available in parts due to inevitable DMCA takedowns (not to mention Google's own subversive purging of "unacceptable" material down the memory hole). So how can WB/Disney/etc. be effectively pressured to stop being pussies and show us some uncensored Tom Cat?
I'm sick of PC censorship of classic cartoons. What can be done to pressure the studios to release uncut versions on DVD?

The most effective way would probably be to distribute "complete", "uncensored" pirated collections. When they notice there is interest in those, they'll be afraid of loosing money that could be made and might change their opinion.

Modern viewing audiences aren't the people interested in Tom and Jerry to begin with. It's obviously going to be something that mainly people with a nostalgic interest or coll.ectors would like. At the very least they should include them as bonus features and slap some dumb warning in front of it about how it doesn't reflect the company's current values and is being presented for historical reference purposes only.
